_comment: Regression tolerance for the end-to-end CPU gate (tools/measure_e2e_cpu.py + tools/check_bench_regression.py --value-key cpu_ms_per_media_s). Separate file from tools/bench-tolerance.json because the unit, the noise floor and the producer are all different.
_why_not_5_percent: docs/04 §8 sets 'end-to-end CPU regression > 5% fails'. Measured on this machine with one binary and no code change, that number is below the noise floor: single runs of the 1080p30 10 s clip spanned 43.1-53.2 ms per media second (8-16%), and the medians of two consecutive groups of five runs differed by 8.1%. The noise is PROPORTIONAL, not a fixed start-up cost -- it did not shrink when the clip got 3x heavier -- so it cannot be removed by measuring a longer clip or by dropping the first seconds. Enforced at 5%, this gate would fire on the machine and not on the tree, which is the one failure mode a gate must not have: it teaches the next person to override it. 5% stays as the design target in docs/04 §8; this file is the machine threshold.
_what_15_percent_still_catches: The regressions this gate exists for (docs/08 R3: a layer starting to charge for itself -- an allocation per frame, a queue that copies instead of moves, a decoder fallback that silently picks software) move CPU by tens of percent, not by 8%. A 15% floor still catches them; what it gives up is the ability to see a 10% drift, which this machine cannot distinguish from its own load.
_what_this_is_not: A noise floor, not a release line. It says 'a delta below this cannot be attributed to the code on this machine'. It does not say the slowdown is acceptable.
_cross_machine: The committed baseline was measured on macOS with VideoToolbox hardware decode; CI runs Linux with VAAPI (or software). Absolute CPU per media second is NOT comparable across machines, so CI records and uploads the JSONL and does not fail on it -- same policy as the micro-benchmark baseline. --fail-on-regression is for a developer's own machine, where before/after are the same box.
